title: Prediction of the Progression of Undifferentiated Arthritis to Rheumatoid Arthritis Using DNA Methylation Profiling.
authors: de la Calle-Fabregat, Carlos; Niemantsverdriet, Ellis; Canete, Juan D; Li, Tianlu; van der Helm-van Mil, Annette H M; Rodriguez-Ubreva, Javier; Ballestar, Esteban
one_liner_zh: 该文利用DNA甲基化谱和机器学习预测未分化关节炎向类风湿关节炎的进展，虽涉及转录因子关联，但核心是表观遗传临床分类，无蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The term "undifferentiated arthritis (UA)" is used to refer to all cases of arthritis that do not fit a specific diagnosis. A significant percentage of UA patients progress to rheumatoid arthritis (RA), others to a different definite rheumatic disease, and the rest undergo spontaneous remission. Therapeutic intervention in patients with UA can delay or halt disease progression and its long-term consequences. It is therefore of inherent interest to identify those UA patients with a high probability of progressing to RA who would benefit from early appropriate therapy. This study was undertaken to investigate whether alterations in the DNA methylation profiles of immune cells may provide information on the genetically or environmentally determined status of patients and potentially discriminate between disease subtypes. METHODS: We performed DNA methylation profiling of a UA patient cohort, in which progression to RA occurred for a significant proportion of the patients. RESULTS: We found differential DNA methylation in UA patients compared to healthy controls. Most importantly, our analysis identified a DNA methylation signature characteristic of those UA cases that differentiated to RA. We demonstrated that the methylome of peripheral mononuclear cells can be used to anticipate the evolution of UA to RA, and that this methylome is associated with a number of inflammatory pathways and transcription factors. Finally, we designed a machine learning strategy for DNA methylation-based classification that predicts the differentiation of UA toward RA. CONCLUSION: Our findings indicate that DNA methylation profiling provides a good predictor of UA-to-RA progression to anticipate targeted treatments and improve clinical management.
abstract_zh: 目的：“未分化关节炎（UA）”这一术语用于指所有不符合特定诊断的关节炎病例。相当比例的UA患者进展为类风湿关节炎（RA），另一些则发展为其他明确的风湿性疾病，其余患者自发缓解。对UA患者进行治疗干预可延缓或阻止疾病进展及其长期后果。因此，识别那些进展为RA概率高、可能受益于早期适当治疗的UA患者具有内在意义。本研究旨在探讨免疫细胞DNA甲基化谱的改变是否能提供关于患者遗传或环境决定状态的信息，并可能区分疾病亚型。方法：我们对一个UA患者队列进行了DNA甲基化谱分析，其中相当比例的患者进展为RA。结果：我们发现与健康对照相比，UA患者存在差异DNA甲基化。最重要的是，我们的分析识别出了一种特征性的DNA甲基化签名，该签名与那些分化为RA的UA病例相关。我们证明，外周单核细胞的甲基化组可用于预测UA向RA的演变，且该甲基化组与多种炎症通路和转录因子相关。最后，我们设计了一种基于DNA甲基化的机器学习分类策略，用于预测UA向RA的分化。结论：我们的研究结果表明，DNA甲基化谱分析为UA向RA进展提供了良好的预测指标，有助于提前制定靶向治疗并改善临床管理。
